Graduate Admissions
Welcome to the electrical and computer engineering graduate program! This page provides key information on the admissions process, including application requirements, deadlines, and supporting materials. Review these guidelines carefully and contact ecengradprograms@tamu.edu with any questions. Our goal is to help you navigate your application and join the Aggie engineering community with confidence.
College-Level Graduate Admission Requirements
All graduate engineering applications will be submitted using EngineeringCAS, a centralized application service.
College-Level Graduate Admissions
Please read the following information regarding the application process for the electrical and computer engineering graduate program. If your question is not answered below, please email our graduate program.
Thank you for your interest in the Electrical and Computer Engineering graduate program.
Please note that this information is the most current and accurate available.
Application
You will apply using EngineeringCAS. You can start uploading documents as soon as you start your application.
Do NOT submit your application until all materials are received.
When you are looking for our applications, please use the following filters:
Available programs
Institution-Texas A&M University
Once you submit your application and pay the fee, you will no longer be able to make changes to your application. We cannot delete files.
Application Fee
You will be required to pay the following fees:
Texas A&M application fee ($65 for domestic students, $90 for international)
Engineering CAS application fee ($58)
Application Deadlines
Spring Applications
Domestic (US Citizen or Permanent Resident): October 1
International (Everyone else, no matter the visa type or where you are going to school): July 1
Fall Applications
Domestic (US Citizen or Permanent Resident): May 1
International (Everyone else, no matter the visa type or where you are going to school): February 1
Distance Program Applications: December 1 (Priority Deadline: November 15) (Spring) and July 15 (Fall)
Quick Admit Applications (Texas A&M Students ONLY): December 1st (Spring) and August 1st (Fall)
To be considered for Electrical and Computer Engineering departmental fellowships, please submit your CAS application by no later than February 1.
Transcripts
Upload unofficial copies of your transcripts to Engineering CAS.
Transcripts can be uploaded under
Program Materials
Documents
If your transcripts are not in English, you must also provide the translation.
WES is NOT required
Please do NOT order a WES Evaluation for this application. You may provide it in addition to the actual transcript if you already have it.
Please enter your GPA exactly as it is listed on your transcript. There is no need to convert it to a 4.0 scale.
Do not mail documents directly to ECEN.
If you are admitted, you will need to provide official transcripts (not evaluations) to Texas A&M before you can register for classes.
Official Test Scores
The department prefers official scores. Engineering CAS and the College of Engineering do not stress this. When applying to Electrical and Computer Engineering, please follow departmental preferences.
The GRE is optional for all applicants. Be aware that applicants with a lower GPA or from a school that our department may not be familiar with may benefit from providing strong GRE scores.
Use code 6003 to report GRE scores for non-engineering programs (Department code is not required). Use code 4119 to report your GRE score for engineering programs.
Applicants whose native languages are not English must fulfill an English proficiency requirement. Use code B887 to send your TOEFL scores.
IELTS Academic scores must be reported directly to Texas A&M University. Instructions for sending the IELTS only can be found on Admissions website under Required Documents.
If you sent the scores to 6003, you do not need to resend them. Please ensure that your unofficial scores are listed on your application if you have not already done so.
For more information on sending your scores, check out the Admissions website.
Statement of Purpose/Personal Statement
Develop a Statement of Purpose/Personal Statement that addresses why you are pursuing a graduate degree in your field of interest, background, and long-term goals. Mention what faculty member you may want to work with if applying for a Thesis/Research-oriented degree. Please try to limit this to no more than a page and a half.
Letters of Recommendation
Graduate applicants are required to submit a minimum of three recommendations, with a maximum of five, from individuals familiar with their academic achievements and potential. For those applying to the distance programs, the requirement is reduced to a minimum of two recommendations. The deadline for the letters is the same as the application deadline. It is not later. These MUST be sent through the Engineering CAS system to be added to your application. No other letters will be accepted.
Funding
For information on funding, see the Graduate Funding Opportunities Page.
More Information:
Please note that this information is provided to enable you to explore all aspects of our program. We recommend visiting our website and researching the area of interest to you. Pull up the faculty members you are interested in working with and look at their CVs. Go to the main Texas A&M University website and search for the research you are interested in. This will often reveal the researchers, their publications, and the groups they work with.
If your background is not in ECE, indicate that clearly in your application. If you are admitted, you will need to reach out to the area you are admitted to and ask them if you need to take any leveling courses. The Graduate Office can provide you with a general list, but the faculty in the area you are admitted to will be able to assist you with what classes you need to take.
